The key control flow is already visible. In `_Transform._walk`, when iterating a dict, the `Fn::ForEach` arm expands the body by calling `_walk(v[2], {**params, **{v[0]: collection_value}}, cfn)` once per collection element. In the test template, the collection is `["X", "Y"]`, so the body is walked twice.

Inside that body:
- `MappedA` contains `{"Fn::FindInMap": ["M", {"Ref": "L"}, "v"]}`. The `Fn::FindInMap` arm constructs `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap(get_hash(v), v)`, so this reachable 3-element list does instantiate `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap`.
- `Wrapped` contains `{"Fn::ToJsonString": {...}}`. The `Fn::ToJsonString` arm immediately `return obj` and does not recurse into its value. That means the nested `trap -> Fn::FindInMap` is preserved untouched and never reaches the `Fn::FindInMap` dispatch in `_walk`.

I still need the class definitions around `_ForEachValueFnFindInMap.__init__` and `_FnFindInMapDefaultValue.__init__` to confirm the only call site is guarded by `if len(obj) == 4`.
